title: canary-rollout-scratchpad-ethan-wright
content:
Personal scratchpad for upcoming canary release (v3.2.0 -> v3.3.0). Notes to self and rough checklist. NOT FINAL.

Goal:
- Gradual rollout of v3.3.0 (kv-cache improvements + kernel fallback) to hosted API and dedicated pools. Verify latency regresses <= 5% and error rate stable.

Quick plan (rough ramp):
- 00:00 UTC deploy to control-plane (config only)
- 00:30 UTC push model binary to staging nodes (staging pool)
- 01:00 UTC smoke tests + perf harness (script: tools/perf/run_canary.sh)
- 02:00 UTC release to 1% traffic (hosted): route policy = latency-first, fallback enabled to v3.2.0
- 04:00 UTC -> 5% if green (metrics below)
- 08:00 UTC -> 20% if green
- 24:00 UTC -> 50% then schedule full at 72h

Pinning notes:
- customers with pinning: ensure route override honored. Config key: routing.pinned_version in DB (see JIRA-RL-421).
- migration: if customer requests rollback, must be able to pin back to v3.2.0 within 1 minute. Test with pinned route e2e test.

Observability / metrics to watch (alerts + dashboards):
- 99p latency (token-level) by model variant (query via metrics: latency_ms{model="gptx-16b"})
- success_rate / error_rate (5m) - alert if > 0.5% increase vs baseline
- token throughput (tokens/s) by pool -> watch for batching anomalies
- KV cache hit ratio (new kernel) - expect +10-20% for chat workloads
- CPU/GPU utilization (per-pool) - alert if sustained > 85%
- Canaries per-region: ensure no region-specific regressions (eu-west, us-west, ap-south)

Smoke tests (staging):
- basic generation (deterministic seed)
- long-context (>2048 tokens) streaming stability
- function calling pattern (tools) - validate structured output remains unchanged
- fallback test: simulate infra failure on canary nodes and verify automatic routing to v3.2.0 within 30s

Rollback plan (fast):
- If latency spike OR error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 30m -> immediate traffic rollback to v3.2.0 via routing change (infra: routing-service-set --version v3.2.0)
- Notify SRE + Release ENG in #releases channel, schedule postmortem if >30m impact

Open questions / TODOs (ask Maya/Noah):
- Are we including quantization profile Q2 with this canary? (Maya thinks yes but want to confirm perf matrix)
- Confirm Dedicated burst policy: will new runtime respect reserved pool limits? (Noah to verify with infra)
- Add canary-specific billing metric to track per-token cost delta vs baseline (product request)

Tasks checklist:
- [ ] Finalize rollout doc and runbook (this file -> move to shared_drives/release-engineering)
- [ ] Create canary job in CI: ci/canary/v3.3.0 (PR created: serving-runtime#842) -> link tests
- [ ] Add dashboard widgets (canary overlay) on per-route console
- [ ] Schedule page for 00:00 UTC deploy (ops calendar)
- [ ] Run dry-run in staging and collect perf traces (trace id prefix: canary-ethan-)

Communication plan:
- Pre-announcement to internal: #releases, uptime-oncall, product-owners 24h before
- Post-deploy status updates every ramp step (automated via slack-bot if possible)

Notes to self:
- keep an eye on seq-length distribution - new kernel favors long-context but may regress short-chat tail latency
- if we see regression confined to one model architecture, consider split by model variant instead of global rollout

Reference commands:
- routing roll forward: infractl routing set --route hosted-api --version v3.3.0 --policy gradual --initial 1
- rollback: infractl routing set --route hosted-api --version v3.2.0 --force

Past canary links (for pattern):
- canary notes (Nov 2025): users/canary-rollout-scratchpad-noah-kim.json

End of scratchpad. Will turn into formal checklist + runbook after dry-run.
